candidate_orders.rationale: business_operations.project-delivery verbatim: 'this is the row in the family with the least doubt about its natural order - the project first, then the document function, then the reporting period last', because 'a status report for week 14 is meaningless before the project is known, exactly as 00's own Homework 3 is meaningless before the course.' The period is last and never first: 'a period-first tree would scatter one project's charter, plan and closure across three calendar folders.'

dimensions.retrieval_rationale: The bounded effort is what a delivery, research or sourcing document belongs to; every row using this recipe names it as the level nothing else is intelligible beneath. 00's parent-before-child rule states it: 'a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.'
Charter, plan, status report, closure, findings pack: what the document DOES is the leaf a person searches for once the effort that produced it is fixed.

A reporting or review interval separates one week's status report from the next inside a single effort. It sits last because the effort outlives it, and it goes unbound where the corpus does not report on a cadence.

candidate_orders.rationale: THE FAMILY DEFAULT, and it is attested rather than invented. The business_operations schema anchor states the family's nesting in its own words: 'the organisational unit or entity only where the corpus really spans more than one ..., then the governance body, project, contract, or account that the material belongs to, then the fiscal period, then the document function.' With organization destination-INELIGIBLE (60 section 4) that paragraph reduces to exactly this order. business_operations.project-delivery's own open_question records the divergence and refuses to close it: 'This row recommends project then document function then reporting period; the schema row's default for the family is body-or-project then fiscal period then function. The inversion is argued in the memo and is deliberate, but it is a narrow difference and R1c should confirm it rather than inherit it.' A recipe whose own corpus calls the difference narrow and asks for confirmation has two attested nestings, not one, and sections 5.3 and 5.8 make choosing between them the user's decision. This is the order for a holder who runs several efforts on one reporting cadence and navigates by the round - 'what went out in Q2' - rather than by the effort.

dimensions.retrieval_rationale: The bounded effort still leads under both orders. Neither the row nor the schema anchor puts anything above it once the entity level is gone, and a period-first tree is refused by both.
The schema anchor's third level, rising above the document function: a holder reporting on a fixed cadence looks for the round first and the kind of paper second.
The document function becomes the leaf, which is where the family default puts it and where project-delivery's inversion moves it from.

refusals.row_sentence: the constituted BODY first (it is the thing a secretary actually files by, and unlike an entity name it is not the collector level 00's template validator rejects), then the meeting occurrence or cycle, then the document function
refusals.why_no_template: business_operations declares no key for a constituted body. `organization` is the entity rather than the board and is destination-INELIGIBLE on the key (60 section 4, section 9.1); binding the body to `project` would contradict the row, whose whole discriminator is that a board is a standing cycle and not a bounded effort.

refusals.row_sentence: The period is genuinely wanted here and is the one level a finance user reliably asks for, but it still should not be first.
refusals.why_no_template: The row's first level is 'the organisational unit or cost centre that owns the plan'. `organization` is destination-INELIGIBLE, so the only remaining order puts the planning round at the root - the one position the row forbids in the sentence quoted. Authoring the reverse would invert the row's stated period-above-function ordering instead. Both available shapes contradict the row, so neither is authored.

refusals.row_sentence: the counterparty or the contract itself, then the agreement or contract reference where one counterparty has several, then the document function
refusals.why_no_template: The counterparty is `client` on the sell side and `supplier` on the buy side, and one contract register holds both roles - the same defect 60 B3 warns about when it records that 'a consignment note routinely names consignor, consignee and carrier in three different roles on one page'. Binding one of the two would file half the corpus under a role it does not have, and business_operations declares no key for the agreement itself.

refusals.row_sentence: the site or building, then the asset, area, or service it concerns, then the document function
